questions.q: If the circles ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 6x + 8y + 16 = 0$ and ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2\left(3 - \sqrt{3}\right)x + 2\left(4 - \sqrt{6}\right)y = k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}$, $k > 0$, touch internally at the point $P\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$, then ${\left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
The circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 6x + 8y + 16 = 0$ has centre $\left(- 3, - 4\right)$ and radius $\sqrt{9 + 16 - 16} = 3$ units.

The circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2\left(3 - \sqrt{3}\right)x + 2\left(4 - \sqrt{6}\right)y =$ $k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}, k > 0$ has centre $\left(\sqrt{3} - 3, \sqrt{6} - 4\right)$ and radius $\sqrt{{\left(\sqrt{3} - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(\sqrt{6} - 4\right)}^{2} + k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{k + 34}$

Given that these two circles touch internally, so

distance between their centres$= \left|\text{difference of radii}\right|$

$\sqrt{3 + 6} = \left|\sqrt{k + 34} - 3\right|$

$⇒ \sqrt{k + 34} - 3 = \pm 3$

Here, $k = 2$ is only possible value $\left(∵ k > 0\right)$

Now the equation of common tangent to both the circles is given by $2\sqrt{3}x + 2\sqrt{6}y + 16 + k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6} = 0$

$∵ k = 2$ then equation becomes

$x + \sqrt{2}y + 3\sqrt{3} + 3 + 4\sqrt{2} = 0 ⋯ \left(i\right)$

$∵ \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ are foot of perpendicular from $\left(- 3, - 4\right)$ to this common tangent, then

$\dfrac{\alpha + 3}{1} = \dfrac{\beta + 4}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{- \left(- 3 - 4\sqrt{2} + 3 + 4\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{3}\right)}{1 + 2}$

$∴ \alpha + 3 = - \sqrt{3} \text{ and } \dfrac{\beta + 4}{\sqrt{2}} = - \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2} = 9$ and ${\left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)}^{2} = 16$

Hence, ${\left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)}^{2} = 25$

questions.q: A rectangle $R$ with end points of the one of its sides as $\left(1, 2\right)$ and $\left(3, 6\right)$ is inscribed in a circle. If the equation of a diameter of the circle is $2x - y + 4 = 0$, then the area of $R$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Equation of line $AB$ will be

$y - 2 = 2\left(x - 1\right)$$⇒ 2x - y = 0$

Now the given diameter is parallel to $AB$

Then, the distance between diameter and line $AB$

$= \left(\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5}}$

Thus, $BC = 2 \times \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$

Also $AB = \sqrt{{\left(1 - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 6\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$

Area of the rectangle$= AB \times BC = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}} \times 2\sqrt{5} = 16$

questions.q: Let the mirror image of a circle ${c}_{1}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x - 6y + \alpha = 0$  in line $y = x + 1$ be ${c}_{2}: 5{x}^{2} + 5{y}^{2} + 10gx$ $+ 10fy + 38 = 0$. If $r$ is the radius of circle ${c}_{2}$, then $\alpha + 6{r}^{2}$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
Let the mirror image of a circle ${c}_{1}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 2x - 6y + \alpha = 0$ in line $y = x + 1$ be ${c}_{2}: 5{x}^{2} + 5{y}^{2} + 10gx$ $+ 10fy + 38 = 0$. If $r$ is the radius of circle ${c}_{2}$, then $\alpha + 6{r}^{2}$ is equal to ______

Now Image of centre ${c}_{1} ≡ \left(1, 3\right)$ in $x - y + 1 = 0$ is given by

$\dfrac{{x}_{1} - 1}{1} = \dfrac{{y}_{1} - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{- 2\left(1 - 3 + 1\right)}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ {x}_{1} = 2, {y}_{1} = 2$

So, centre of circle ${c}_{2} ≡ \left(2, 2\right)$

Now radius of circle ${c}_{2}$ will be $\sqrt{4 + 4 - \dfrac{38}{5}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}} = r$

Now $\left(\text{radius of}{{c}_{1}}^{2}\right) =$${\left(\text{radius of}{c}_{2}\right)}^{2}$ as they are image to one another,

$⇒ \sqrt{{1}^{2} + {3}^{2} - \alpha} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}$

$⇒ 10 - \alpha = \dfrac{2}{5} ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{48}{5}$

Now putting the value of $\alpha \text{ and } r$ in $\alpha + 6{r}^{2}$ we get,

$\alpha + 6{r}^{2} = \dfrac{48}{5} + \dfrac{12}{5} = 12$

questions.q: Consider a circle ${C}_{1}: x{}^{2} + {y}^{2} – 4x – 2y = \alpha – 5 .$ Let its mirror image in the line $y = 2x + 1$ be another circle ${C}_{2}: 5{x}^{2} + 5{y}^{2} – 10fx – 10gy + 36 = 0 .$  Let $r$ be the radius of ${C}_{2}$ . Then $\alpha + r$ is equal to $________$
questions.solution:
Given,

${C}_{1}: {x}_{2} + {y}_{2} – 4x – 2y + \left(5 – \alpha\right) = 0$

So, its centre will be, ${O}_{1} = \left(2, 1\right)$ and radius $= \sqrt{\alpha}$

And ${C}_{2}: 5{x}^{2} + 5{y}^{2} – 10fx – 10gy + 36 = 0$

$⇒ {C}_{2}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} – 2fx – 2gy + \dfrac{36}{5} = 0$

So, Centre ${O}_{2} = \left(f, g\right)$ and radius $r = \sqrt{{f}^{2} + {g}^{2} - \dfrac{36}{5}}$

Also given ${O}_{2}$ is reflection of ${O}_{1}$ in $2x – y + 1 = 0$, so image formula we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{f - 2}{2} = \dfrac{g - 1}{- 1} = - 2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{2 \times 2 - 1 + 1}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f = \dfrac{- 6}{5}$ and $g = \dfrac{13}{5}$

So, radius $r = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{- 6}{5}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{13}{5}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{36}{5}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{25}}{5} = 1$

$⇒ r = 1$and $\alpha = 1$ as they both are same radius circle,

Hence, $r + \alpha = 2$.

questions.q: Let the abscissae of the two points $P$ and $Q$ be the roots of $2{x}^{2} - rx + p = 0$ and the ordinates of $P$ and $Q$ be the roots of ${x}^{2} - sx - q = 0$. If the equation of the circle described on $PQ$ as diameter is $2\left({x}^{2} + {y}^{2}\right) - 11x - 14y - 22 = 0$, then $2r + s - 2q + p$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let the roots of $2{x}^{2} - rx + p = 0$ are ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}$ and roots of ${y}^{2} - sy - q = 0$ are ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}$

So, ${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} = \dfrac{r}{2}, {x}_{1}{x}_{2} = \dfrac{p}{2}, {y}_{1} + {y}_{2} = s, {y}_{1}{y}_{2} = - q$

Equation of the circle with $PQ$ as diameter will be

$\left(x - {x}_{1}\right)\left(x - {x}_{2}\right) + \left(y - {y}_{1}\right)\left(y - {y}_{2}\right) = 0$

i.e. $2\left({x}^{2} + {y}^{2}\right) - rx - 2sy + p - 2q = 0$

On comparing with the given equation $r = 11, s = 7$

$p - 2q = - 22$

$∴ 2r + s - 2q + p = 22 + 7 - 22 = 7$

questions.q: An ellipse $E: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ passes through the vertices of the hyperbola $H: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{49} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{64} = - 1$. Let the major and minor axes of the ellipse $E$ coincide with the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola $H$. Let the product of the eccentricities of $E$ and $H$ be $\dfrac{1}{2}$. If $l$ is the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $E$, then the value of $113l$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

Hyperbola:$\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{64} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{49} = 1$

And ellipse $E: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ passes through the vertices of the hyperbola $H: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{49} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{64} = - 1$, so vertices will be $V ≡ \left(0, \pm 8\right)$

So ${b}^{2} = 64$

Now eccentricity of hyperbola will be ${e}_{H} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{49}{64}}$

And eccentricity of ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ will be

${e}_{E} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{64}}$

And using $b = 8$

We get, ${e}_{H} \times {e}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (given)

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - {a}^{2}}{64}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{113}}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{64 - {a}^{2}} \times \sqrt{113} = 32$

$⇒ \left(64 - {a}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{{32}^{2}}{113}$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = 64 - \dfrac{{32}^{2}}{113}$

Now length of latus rectum will be $l = \dfrac{2{a}^{2}}{b} = \dfrac{2}{8}\left(64 - \dfrac{{32}^{2}}{113}\right) = \dfrac{1552}{113}$

$⇒ 113l = 1552$

questions.q: Let $A\left(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right), a > 0$, be a fixed point in the $xy$-plane. The image of $A$ in $y$-axis be $B$ and the image of $B$ in $x$-axis be $C$. If $D\left(3cos\theta, asin\theta\right)$,  is a point in the fourth quadrant such that the maximum area of $∆ ACD$ is $12$ square units, then $a$ is equal to _____
questions.solution:
$A = \left(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right)$

$B = \left(\dfrac{- 3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right)$ is the image of $A$ on y-axis

$C = \left(- \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, - \sqrt{a}\right)$ is the image of $B$ in x-axis

$D\left(3cos\theta, asin\theta\right)$

Area of triangle $ACD$ will be

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & \sqrt{a} & 1 \\ - \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & - \sqrt{a} & 1 \\ 3cos\theta & asin\theta & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= 3\sqrt{a}\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)$

The maximum area of triangle is $3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2}$

i.e. $3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2} = 12$

$⇒ a = 8$

questions.question: Let $A\left(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right), a > 0$, be a fixed point in the $xy$-plane. The image of $A$ in $y$-axis be $B$ and the image of $B$ in $x$-axis be $C$. If $D\left(3cos\theta, asin\theta\right)$,  is a point in the fourth quadrant such that the maximum area of $∆ ACD$ is $12$ square units, then $a$ is equal to _____
questions.explanation:
$A = \left(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right)$

$B = \left(\dfrac{- 3}{\sqrt{a}}, \sqrt{a}\right)$ is the image of $A$ on y-axis

$C = \left(- \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}}, - \sqrt{a}\right)$ is the image of $B$ in x-axis

$D\left(3cos\theta, asin\theta\right)$

Area of triangle $ACD$ will be

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & \sqrt{a} & 1 \\ - \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{a}} & - \sqrt{a} & 1 \\ 3cos\theta & asin\theta & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= 3\sqrt{a}\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)$

The maximum area of triangle is $3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2}$

i.e. $3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2} = 12$

$⇒ a = 8$

questions.q: A ray of light passing through the point $P\left(2, 3\right)$ reflects on the $X$-axis at point $A$ and the reflected ray passes through the point $Q\left(5, 4\right)$. Let $R$ be the point that divides the line segment $AQ$ internally into the ratio $2: 1$. Let the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular $M$ from $R$ on the bisector of the angle $PAQ$ be $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$. Then, the value of $7\alpha + 3\beta$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
By observation we know the point $A\left(\alpha, 0\right)$ and $\beta = y$-coordinate of $R$$= \dfrac{2 \times 4 + 1 \times 0}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{8}{3} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now ${P}^{'}$ is image of $P$ in $y = 0$ which will be ${P}^{'}\left(2, - 3\right)$

$∴$ Equation of ${P}^{'}Q$ is $\left(y + 3\right) = \dfrac{4 + 3}{5 - 2}\left(x - 2\right)$

i.e. $3y + 9 = 7x - 14$

Now ${P}^{'}Q$ meets $x -$axis at $A$

so $A ≡ \left(\dfrac{23}{7}, 0\right)$ by solving with $y = 0$

$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{23}{7} ⋯ \left(2\right)$

By $\left(1\right), \left(2\right)$, we get

$7\alpha + 3\beta = 23 + 8 = 31$

questions.q: A triangle is formed by $X$-axis, $Y$-axis and the line $3x + 4y = 60$. Then the number of points $P\left(a, b\right)$ which lie strictly inside the triangle, where $a$ is an integer and $b$ is a multiple of $a$, is _____ .
questions.solution:
Given:

$3x + 4y = 60$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{20} + \dfrac{y}{15} = 1$

If $x = 1, y = \dfrac{57}{4} = 14 . 25$

So, points are

$\left(1, 1\right)\left(1, 2\right) - \left(1, 14\right) ⇒ 14$ points.

If $x = 2, y = \dfrac{27}{2} = 13 . 5$

So, points are

$\left(2, 2\right)\left(2, 4\right) \ldots \left(2, 12\right) ⇒ 6$ points.

If $x = 3, y = \dfrac{51}{4} = 12 . 75$

So, points are

$\left(3, 3\right)\left(3, 6\right) - \left(3, 12\right) ⇒ 4$ points.

If $x = 4, y = 12$

So, points are

$\left(4, 4\right)\left(4, 8\right) ⇒ 2$ points.

If $x = 5, y = \dfrac{45}{4} = 11 . 25$

So, points are

$\left(5, 5\right), \left(5, 10\right) ⇒ 2$ points.

If $x = 6, y = \dfrac{21}{2} = 10 . 5$

So, point is

$\left(6, 6\right) ⇒ 1$ point

If $x = 7, y = \dfrac{39}{4} = 9 . 75$

So, point is

$\left(7, 7\right) ⇒ 1$ point

If $x = 8, y = 9$

So, point is

$\left(8, 8\right) ⇒$ $1$ point

If $x = 9 ⇒ y = \dfrac{33}{4} = 8 . 25 ⇒$ no point

Total points inside the triangle

$= 31$ points
